reason: The problem is real and the seat's numbers are exact -- driven in chromium at 390x844 the date stamp measures 24-297 at top 192, .reading .rule renders 309-366 (57px) at top 199 with nothing to its right, and 'Twelve weeks' drops to 24-115 at top 241; the wrap zone is 320-476 and again 561-580 where the rail returns and steals width. But the finding is REFUTED on its fix, which does not do what it claims. Applied verbatim (gap-tight, .rule display:none, .reading p:not(:last-child)::after {content:' ·'}) and re-measured, the reading does NOT become a single line: the first stamp grows to 24-312 and 'Twelve weeks' still sits alone at 24-115 on a second line (container 106px vs 110px before). The fix trades a dangling hairline for a dangling middot -- the ' ·' is stranded at the end of line one at x~297-312 pointing at the same nothing -- so by the seat's own argument it is the same defect in a heavier mark, and the stated goal is unreachable: 273px of date + separator + 91px of 'Twelve weeks' needs ~382px against 342px of content width at 390. The scope is also wrong: max-width:560px leaves the 561-580 band, where the rule is a 124-138px stub at 389-513 with the label on line two, untouched. Severity 'defect' is the right class for the underlying problem -- a 1px zinc-200 stub is visibly wrong and passable, not misleading and not blocking. Nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts on .reading geometry, so this is not a restatement of a proven assertion.
sharpenedFix: Hide the rule across the whole wrap zone and let the two stamps wrap as whole flex items with the separator LEADING the second one, so no mark is ever left at the end of a line. In a new @media (max-width: 600px) block: `.reading { gap: var(--gap-tight); } .reading .rule { display: none; } .reading p:not(:first-child)::before { content: "\00b7\00a0"; }`. Note the selector must be :not(:first-child) or p ~ p -- `p + p` does not match, because span.rule sits between the two paragraphs. Measured: at 390 this yields line one 24-297 and line two '· Twelve weeks' 24-130, no stray mark, container 106px; at 480 and above (including the 561-580 rail band) it joins into one line, 24-297 plus 305-412, container 61px, identical to today's joined reading. 600px is the threshold because the wrap zone measures 320-476 and 561-580; at 601 the rule returns at ~164px, long enough to read as a connector rather than a stub, so there is no jarring jump at the boundary. This also matches house idiom -- the workspace/owner line and the error state's 'Last good reading · ...' already join with a middot.
breaks: Nothing else uses class .rule (single occurrence, lately.html:726), so the display:none is contained. The middot is a decorative pseudo-element inheriting --ink-3 on --paper-2, a pairing already shipped, but re-run audit.mjs anyway for contrast, type-ramp and leading since a new text glyph enters the label voice. Re-run interaction-check.mjs: the reading-instant assertion counts elements with a text child node containing readingLong, and a ::before adds no text node, so it should stay green -- confirm it. The reading block loses ~4px of height (110 -> 106) at 390 and is unchanged at 1440, but it sits in the header above <main>, so re-measure the loading-state skeleton height assertions at 390 (hero and kpi heights are compared skeleton-vs-real and both shift equally, so they should hold). Re-shoot light-full--390x844.png and the 768/1280/1440 frames, and check the dark variant, since the rule is the only --line hairline in the header.
